scope: Proposition 5.4 (Regular evidence) of the manuscript “Almost-everywhere Fourier convergence in L log L” (preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 075 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9a77d41e5b9b9beb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider any finite procedure starting with the type-zero label, making at most ⌊C0h⌋ successful main additions and using the updates of Lemma 5.3 with its hypotheses at every attempt. Require all discrete choices to depend only on spatial prefixes and input memberships, with independent label errors given Y and its parameter path, and include all the success draws specified above. Then an admissible regular attempt has the following conditional reference bound, given its past and its success coin. The observable event for some fresh clone Z′ , A(Z′ − Z) ≤ 4sd, ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ∑︂ x ν(x)vx(Z′ )χgx(V ) ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ≥ β/4. (5.21) has probability at most e−t/8, where Z is the old main label. Under the true input law, all attempted pasts are admissible and Equation (5.21) occurs at every regular success simultaneously, except on a set of probability o(h−20). This includes the label draws at a final success breaching a cap. The bounds are uniform in depth, cutoff, and the deterministic choices made at the states.
